:::{#thm-non-exposed}
#### No exposure means no expected events

For each exposure magnitude $t \ge 0$,
let $Y_t$ be the count observed over exposure $t$.
If the mean count is proportional to the exposure magnitude,
$\E{Y_t} = \rate \cdot t$ for all $t \ge 0$ with one finite rate $\rate$,
then there are no expected events without exposure:

$$\E{Y_0} = 0$$

:::

::: proof
$$
\ba
\E{Y_0}
&= \rate \cdot 0 && (\text{evaluate } \E{Y_t} = \rate t \text{ at } t = 0) \\
&= 0 && (\text{multiplication by zero; } \rate \text{ is finite})
\ea
$$
:::
